questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Learning in a different setting, exploring another culture and making new international connections.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The experience was a 10 minus my accomodations which were not adequate.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, I did manage to be confused anyways but I don't think that was anyone else's fault.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A welcome seminar and a lot of additional information online plus an offer of both virtual and physical assistance from the international office in the university of Vienna.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: It was great!

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy, but I chose poorly. My recommendation is to go to housingAnywhere at least three months in advance and search for a room in a private apartment, and not do the whole dormitory thing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It can be great and not that expensive either. I only lived a 15 minutes walk from campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Find another living situation than Porzellaneum Dormitory.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I registered at the university through Mobility Online and my course through their website U:find.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: My sending university guided me throug it all.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was quite succesful. There was however some courses I did not get that I applied for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply for more classes than ECTS points you need and just deregister in time

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The level was maybe a bit low.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took 4 BA courses and 2 MA courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very different. Attendance and participation was fx mandatory which I have not tried before, it had its strenghts and weaknesses.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Life and Death in Art and Cultural Heritage (Lecture)
Selected Topics in Political Anthropology (Seminar)
New Critical Perspectives in Social and Cultural Anthropology (Lecture)
New Critical Perspectives (Seminar)
Anthropology of Ritual Action (Seminar)
Thinking with Things: Anthropological Approaches to Material Culture (Seminar)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Life and Death in Art and Cultural Heritage (Lecture)
Selected Topics in Political Anthropology (Seminar)
New Critical Perspectives (Seminar)
Anthropology of Ritual Action (Seminar)
Thinking with Things: Anthropological Approaches to Material Culture (Seminar)

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: A lot of additional monetary fees at my accomodation and the buying of all kitchen appliances, pillow and duvet. Nothing was provided other than room, bed and a kitchen without pots, pans and everything else.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The Supermarkets were the same prices as in Denmark although I expected it would be a little bit cheaper. Going out was really cheap compared to Denmark which was great.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds of social gatherings (Octoberfest etc.). Sports courses (I went to an outdoor workout twice a week in a park fx.). And Vienna has a very rich cultural scene with museums, theaters, Operas and so on.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
A free outdoor workout at Arne-Carlsson-Park. It happens two times a week.

Definitely visit the Museums: Welt Museum, Albertina Museum, Kunsthistorische Museum etc.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Travel to Bratislava with bus, very cheap and only takes two hours. 

Skiing, either with Erasmus or friends.

Volksgarten and U4 nightclubs

Museums and concerts.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Meet up at bars near uni or go to uni social events.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I din't find any in particular that difficult. But there definitely is a whole lot of rules which are, I guess, more important that you follow, than they are in Denmark. Austrian's like strictness and rulebooks.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The architecture and beauty of the city.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Apply for private accomodations at least three months before departure.
Remember to prioritize Erasmus events especially in the beginning.
When discovering new places, save them on your Maps app, so you can find them again. There will be a lot of places you will love.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of socialising happens in bars.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The new personal connections I got along the way and the course Selected Topics in Political Anthropology.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The amount of documentation needed from a bunch of different sources.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
